rot.ideia.ex1.e1: You already know: on its first move, a pawn may move two squares.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: If it jumps two squares and stops next to an enemy pawn, it can be captured as if it moved one.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: This is en passant: "in passing", in French. The black pawn just jumped from d7 to d5.
rot.ideia.ex1.e4: Your pawn goes diagonally to the square the black pawn jumped over.
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! Your pawn went to d6, and the pawn on d5 left the board.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The pawn goes from e5 to d6 and captures the pawn on d5, in passing.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.e5e6.1: The pawn advanced, and the chance to capture is gone.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.e5e6.2: Let's go back: capture the pawn that just jumped.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not capture en passant. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Notice: your pawn did not go to the captured pawn's square, but to the one behind it.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Now as Black. White jumped the pawn from c2 to c4, next to yours.
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: Perfect! Your pawn went to c3, and the pawn on c4 left the board.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The pawn goes from d4 to c3 and captures the pawn on c4, in passing.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d4d3.1: The pawn advanced, and the chance to capture is gone.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d4d3.2: Let's go back: capture the pawn that just jumped.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not capture en passant. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: Careful: it only works on the move right after the jump. And only pawn against pawn.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Now I will show the right that runs out and the pawn that tries to escape by jumping.
rot.demos.acaba.e1: The black pawn on f7 is going to jump two squares, next to the white pawn.
rot.demos.acaba.l1: Done: now White can capture en passant.
rot.demos.acaba.l2: The capture is not compulsory. Here, White prefers another move.
rot.demos.acaba.l4: Now it no longer works: the right lasted only that one move.
rot.demos.fuga.e1: The white pawn wants to get past the black pawn without being captured.
rot.demos.fuga.l1: It jumps two squares, over a3, the square the black pawn attacks.
rot.demos.fuga.l2: It does not help: the black pawn captures in passing and goes to a3.
rot.demos.fuga.l3: That is what en passant is for: the two-square jump does not escape a pawn alongside.
rot.demos.fuga.l4: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, as White and as Black, capture en passant.
rot.pratica.brancas.enunciado: The black pawn just jumped from c7 to c5. Capture en passant.
rot.pratica.brancas.fim: Well done. The pawn went to the square behind the captured one.
rot.pratica.brancas.err.b5b6: The pawn advanced, and the chance is gone. Try again.
rot.pratica.pretas.enunciado: As Black: White jumped the pawn from f2 to f4. Capture en passant.
rot.pratica.pretas.fim: Perfect. Now you know the most curious rule in chess.
rot.pratica.pretas.err.g4g3: The pawn advanced, and the chance is gone. Try again.
